answer: Agents can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may place orders, then slash that stake when independent audits prove coordinated duplicate identities are manipulating trades. A real operator can spread capital across accounts, but each new persona needs its own locked funds and risks losing them, so cheap identity creation no longer yields cheap influence. The sparrow, mesa, and prism markets can all apply the same rule, making a Sybil swarm costly to maintain.
